title: Why AI is moving from air to liquid
sources: Uptime Institute, Global Data Center Survey (2026)

scenes.say: The newest AI chips run so hot that fans can't cool them. So data centres are turning into plumbing.
scenes.caption: The newest AI chips run so hot that fans can't cool them. So data centres are turning into plumbing.

scenes.say: A normal server rack draws about eleven kilowatts. Nvidia's newest AI rack packs seventy-two chips tightly together, so they work as one giant chip. It draws about a hundred and twenty.
scenes.caption: A normal server rack draws about 11 kilowatts. Nvidia's newest AI rack packs 72 chips tightly together, so they work as one giant chip. It draws about 120.

scenes.say: Every watt becomes heat. And air can only carry away about twenty kilowatts per rack.
scenes.caption: Every watt becomes heat. And air can only carry away about 20 kilowatts per rack.

scenes.say: Litre for litre, water holds about thirty-five hundred times more heat than air. So cold plates now sit right on the chips. Or whole servers sink into a fluid that doesn't conduct electricity.
scenes.caption: Litre for litre, water holds about 3,500 times more heat than air. So cold plates now sit right on the chips. Or whole servers sink into a fluid that doesn't conduct electricity.

scenes.say: Does that mean more water? Not if the loop is closed. Microsoft says its zero-evaporation design saves a hundred and twenty-five million litres a year, per site.
scenes.caption: Does that mean more water? Not if the loop is closed. Microsoft says its zero-evaporation design saves 125 million litres a year, per site.

scenes.say: In hot, humid India, operators like Yotta already run their AI chips on liquid.
scenes.caption: In hot, humid India, operators like Yotta already run their AI chips on liquid.

scenes.say: So, next time you hear AI data centre, ask: how is it cooled? And where does the heat go?
scenes.caption: So next time you hear "AI data centre", ask: how is it cooled? And where does the heat go?
